description: Cross-domain pressure cases for the root-cause-investigation skill. Each case tests whether the skill preserves evidence/mechanism/action discipline while adapting domain vocabulary, evidence sources, controls, and gates.

cases.prompt: Use the root cause investigation panel. We keep having serious failures in our process and need to know the root cause. Please do the RCA.

required_patterns.description: Asks for missing event, consequence, system boundary, evidence, uncertainty, recurrence question, or authority before selecting a method.
required_patterns.pattern: (case frame|event definition|consequence|system boundary|evidence inventory|known uncertainty|action authority|minimum missing)

required_patterns.description: Treats method choice as provisional or says there is not enough input to choose yet.
Classifies missing evidence as blocking, material, or optional.
Requests a small number of decision-relevant missing inputs.

cases.failure_pattern: identity and evidence context lost across service boundaries
cases.prompt: Use the root cause investigation panel. A multi-agent product works in direct chat, but scheduled wake executions sometimes complete in the wrong conversation or without evidence refs. Recent fixes make simple wake pass, but complex multi-tool wakes still produce occasional exact-response failures. Investigate across runtime, workboard, shell delivery, and agent profile boundaries.

required_patterns.description: Separates current defects from historical/fixed observations.
Maps fields to producers, consumers, owner surfaces, or survival tests.
Names file, function, module, route, or interface-level owners where evidence supports it.
Requires machine-readable scenario evidence before accepting a pass.
Preserves code/model division for semantic fulfillment.
Includes runnable gates, commands, artifacts, or pass/fail conditions.

cases.failure_pattern: lot identity and inspection context lost between production and QA
cases.prompt: Use the root cause investigation panel. A packaged food line shipped three pallets with incorrect allergen labels. Production records say the labels were correct at line start, QA inspection passed the first case, and the warehouse scan shows the affected pallets share a partial lot code. Maintenance replaced a labeler sensor during the shift. Build an RCA that can guide containment and recurrence prevention.

required_patterns.description: Uses manufacturing-appropriate methods such as timeline, change analysis, Ishikawa/6M, barrier analysis, or FMEA.
Requires lot genealogy, scan records, inspection records, sensor maintenance, or batch evidence.
Includes containment, hold, recall scope, or segregation controls.
Treats fishbone categories as evidence-tagged hypotheses, not conclusions.
Defines verification signals for corrective actions.

cases.failure_pattern: medication context lost during patient handoff
cases.prompt: Use the root cause investigation panel. A patient received a duplicate anticoagulant dose after transfer from the emergency department to the inpatient floor. The ED note mentioned a held medication, the MAR showed an active order, and the verbal handoff was interrupted twice. No permanent harm occurred, but it was a near miss requiring a safety review.

required_patterns.description: Uses safety timeline, barrier analysis, human factors, Swiss cheese, or just-culture framing.
Requires MAR, orders, chart notes, handoff details, staffing/context, or protocol evidence.
Avoids blaming an individual and treats human action as system context.
Identifies prevention/detection/recovery controls.
Separates what is known from disputed or missing evidence.

forbidden_patterns: human error was the root cause

cases.failure_pattern: approval metadata lost between workflow and payment execution
cases.prompt: Use the root cause investigation panel. A vendor payment above the approval threshold was executed without the required second approval visible in the audit package. The workflow tool shows a second approver clicked approve, but the payment ledger has only one approver ID. Reconciliation caught it two days later. Investigate as an operational control failure, not a fraud accusation.

required_patterns.description: Uses control failure, process map, segregation of duties, reconciliation, or audit trail analysis.
Maps approval metadata from workflow to ledger and audit package.
Avoids unsupported fraud or intent conclusions.
Requires transaction ID, approver IDs, timestamps, ledger refs, and audit artifacts.
Defines a replay/reconciliation/control gate.

cases.failure_pattern: identity context lost between SSO, app session, and audit log
cases.prompt: Use the root cause investigation panel. An internal admin action was recorded in the application audit log as service-account, but SSO logs show a named user initiated a session at the same time. There is no evidence of data exfiltration. Security wants to know whether this is an incident, an observability defect, or both, and what controls should prevent recurrence.

required_patterns.description: Uses timeline, attack-path alternative, control mapping, detection/containment, or identity boundary analysis.
Requires SSO logs, app sessions, service-account mapping, audit log, timestamps, or correlation IDs.
Separates observability defect from security incident hypotheses.
Does not overclaim compromise or exfiltration without evidence.
Defines correlation/replay/detection validation gates.
